name: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
problem: Post-training quality has been getting less attention than pre-training scale, and the distillation/rejection-sampling recipe is the least documented part of frontier pipelines.
mechanism: The distillation link in the Llama 3 pipeline: after pre-training the 405B model, its OUTPUTS are used to post-train smaller Llama 3 models via rejection sampling and preference optimization, giving each size its own data and its own optimizer iteration counts rather than one global recipe. The paper also describes model pruning, distillation-based data curation (LLM-as-judge quality filters on pretraining data), post-training Quantization (FP8 training with BF16 for numerical stability), and scalable infrastructure - i.e. the whole post-training recipe in one document.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): Llama 3 'delivers comparable quality to leading language models such as GPT-4 on a plethora of tasks', with the largest model a dense 405B Transformer with a 128K context window. No per-model distillation delta is given in the abstract - the numeric per-size comparisons are in the paper's tables. The concrete quantization claim relevant to this KB is FP8 post-training quantization, which is a quality-preserving cast rather than a compression method.
